Article Title: Amrinder Singh Raja Warring 'quits' as Punjab Congress chief amid factional feud, changes X bio
Article Text:
Vijay Inder Singla, Pargat Singh, Rana KP Singh and Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria are among those being considered by the high command to replace him, say sources, with Singla emerging as a frontrunner.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Thursday changed his X bio to "former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President" amid speculation that the Congress high command has asked the Ludhiana MP to step down from the top party post in the state amid a factional feud.This comes hours after Warring declined to comment on reports that the party high command had decided to replace him, saying that “some issues are internal”.The move comes after months of infighting within the Punjab Congress, which intensified after the party high command decided on July 1 to retain Warring as the state unit chief.A section of leaders led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi had opposed Warring’s continuation and sought his removal. Leaders aligned with the Channi camp also stayed away from party programmes led by Warring.According to PTI, the Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge held a series of meetings with state leaders before submitting his report to the party high command on the proposed leadership change.The high command subsequently informed Warring of its decision, party sources told PTI, adding that the Congress is now looking to appoint a leader who can bring different factions together ahead of the 2027 assembly polls.Former minister and ex-MP Vijay Inder Singla has emerged as a frontrunner for the post, sources said. The other names being discussed include former Olympian and Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh, former MLA Rana KP Singh, Raja Sansi MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa.The leadership tussle has played out publicly in recent months, raising concerns within the party over its impact on the Congress campaign as it seeks to return to power in Punjab.The factionalism has also added to concerns over the party’s ability to consolidate its organisation ahead of the assembly polls.Asked about the possibility of a change in the Punjab Congress leadership on Tuesday, Channi said the decision was the prerogative of the party high command.“It is the prerogative of Rahul Gandhi and (Mallikarjun) Kharge ji. Only they know who is to be appointed or when is to be changed,” Channi told reporters in Delhi.Warring had also faced criticism from sections of the party over the Congress’ electoral performance in Punjab and his leadership.In August, he defended himself against criticism over the party’s decline in the 2022 assembly elections, questioning attempts to hold him responsible for the loss.“The only mistake is that when the Congress Party had 80 seats, we came down from 80 to 18 seats. Is that my fault? Captain Amarinder Singh led the government twice. From 80 seats, we came down to 18 seats,” he had said.
Article Summary: Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Thursday changed his X bio to "former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President" This comes amid speculation that the Congress high command has asked the Ludhiana MP to step down from the top party post in the state. Vijay Inder Singla, Pargat Singh, Rana KP Singh and Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria are among those being considered.

Article Title: Police were helpless, people feared mafia before 2017: UP CM Yogi
Article Text:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath spoke about the state's challenges and police issues before 2017.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday said that before BJP came into the power in the year 2017, people of UP were disturbed and troubled by the influence of mafia and the police were unable to help the people of the state because they were helpless.The state has experienced a lot of challenges on every front, CM Yogi stated this while attending a flag off ceremony of 87 Interceptor Vehicles equipped with advanced equipment."It was the most populous state yet lagged in the economy, recruitment, the adoption of emerging technologies, and the implementation of welfare schemes. Before 2017, people would immediately dismiss someone simply by labelling them UP-wala. We acknowledge the challenge the police faced; after all, if the political leadership lacks the resolve to make decisions, how can the law and order situation be set right. People would grovel and kneel before the mafia, and the police were helpless," CM stated.Yogi Adityanath said the state has been freed from policy stagnation under his leadership."Since 2017, casting aside that despair and rescuing the state from policy paralysis, we have successfully steered it toward progress.I can now state that we have implemented police reforms...we have installed over 14 lakh cameras in cities...Integrated Command and Control Centres have been established in every district, creating a new identity for them. Furthermore, the objective regarding 'Safe City' traffic initiatives—specifically the deployment of interceptor vehicles—has been realised," he said.UP congress president Ajay Rai visited Gorakhpur to have meeting with the owner of a beauty parlour in Betiahata, whose stocks were submerged due to three days of continuous rain and waterlogging.He stated, "The entire region of Gorakhpur is suffering today, I visited a poor family where a woman is running a beauty parlor on borrowed money to support herself and her family."Congress president, Rai wanted the immediate compensation for the lady, who was affected and the proper action should be taken against the officials, who were responsible for the mismanagement, he added.Rai also wanted an apology to the residents of Gorakhpur from the UP chief minister, Yogi Adityanath.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath said the state has been freed from policy stagnation under his leadership. UP congress president Ajay Rai visited Gorakhpur to have meeting with the owner of a beauty parlour whose stocks were submerged due to three days of continuous rain and waterlogging.

Article Title: 'Indomitable bravery’: Indian Flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar to be awarded ‘Visisht Gujarat Garima Award’
Article Text:
Smit Machhar has been hailed by PM modi, Netanyahu and Trump

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat government on Thursday announced that they will award Indian pilot Smit Machchhar with the 'Visisht Gujarat Garima Award' for fighting his copilot who allegedly planned to crash the plane that was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot while fighting him in the cockpit, but fought back and was severely injured. The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia with all the passengers safe."The courage of Captain Smit Machchhar, the pilot of the flight headed to Israel, is being saluted by the entire world today. Despite being drenched in blood due to the attack, he displayed indomitable bravery to save the lives of 174 passengers—a feat that is profoundly inspiring and commendable," said Gujarat CM Bhupendra Patel on X."This valiant son of Gujarat has illuminated the name of Gujarat and the nation across the globe through his heroism. The Gujarati spirit flowing in his veins fills us all with immense pride. To honor his extraordinary act of bravery and humanity, the Government of Gujarat will bestow upon Captain Smit Machhar the 'Visisht Gujarat Garima Award'," he added.Further praying for his swift recovery, the CM said, "The empathy and prayers of the nation's citizens are with Captain Smit Machchhar."Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed for his courage after being stabbed by his Omani co-pilot during the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump among those praising his actions. PM Modi said Machchhar had shown “remarkable patience, presence of mind, and courage” and described him as a “HERO”, saying his valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a major tragedy.Netanyahu also saluted Machchhar for his “extraordinary bravery”, saying that despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, opened the cockpit door and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker. Trump similarly called the Indian pilot “a hero”, saying that even while badly wounded, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door and call for help.Read more: PM Modi heaps praise on flydubai pilot Captain Machchhar Captain Smit Machchhar, a Mumbaikar from Ghatkopar, is a commercial pilot who trained in New Zealand for his commercial pilot licence and later completed his Boeing 737 type rating at FSTC in Manesar, Gurgaon. He worked with SpiceJet for about a decade before joining flydubai in 2022.Machchhar, who is in his mid-30s, comes from a family with aviation ties, with his brother also working as a flydubai pilot. Friends and former colleagues describe him as a calm, decent and hardworking professional who was always willing to learn. He is currently recovering after being injured in the cockpit attack.Read more: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his Omani co-pilot while fighting him in the cockpit, but fought back and was severely injured. The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia with all the passengers safe. Gujarat CM Bhupendra Patel: "This valiant son of Gujarat has illuminated the name of Gujarat and the nation across the globe"

Article Title: Watch: DYFI activists allegedly attack Kerala minister OJ Janeesh’s car in Kannur

Article Title: Chita Andolan is back: Why are Madhya Pradesh's Panna villagers protesting against Ken-Betwa project
Article Text:
MP dam project: Protesters brave rain and waterlogging for 20th day

What is happening in Madhya Pradesh's Panna?

Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days, with some suffering from wounds on their feet and other skin-related problems. (ANI photo)

So why are the protesters back?

For thousands of tribal families living in the path of the project, it has become a battle over land, forests, livelihoods and identity.

Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations, standing waist-deep in river water, laying beside symbolic funeral pyres and even climbed symbolic gallows.

'Ken-Betwa River Linking Project' is India's first river-linking initiative aimed to transform the drought-prone Bundelkhand region through irrigation, drinking water supply and power generation.

What is the project aiming to accomplish?

Remember the unnerving visuals from Chita Andolan in Madhya Pradesh? Displaced Tribals sleeping on pyres, standing in water for their compensation. The unique protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.Activist Amit Bhatnagar, Jai Kisan Sangathan leader, who has been on a hunger strike for the past four days, was arrested on Wednesday as protesters demonstrated chita, jal, sooli, mitti, bhook (pyre, water, gallows, soil, hunger) other forms of satyagraha.Bhatnagar accused the Panna administration of suppressing the agitation by lathicharging protesters, including women.Speaking to TOI before his arrest, Bhatnagar said, "For the past three days, the police have been bringing along people dressed in plain clothes, who misbehaved with women, entered their homes and even took away people’s phones which have still not been returned. When we approach the police, they ask who took the phones. How are people supposed to identify every face and find out who took them?""There is an atmosphere of fear in the villages. If we say anything, they start resorting to lathi-charge and filing false cases against the protesters," he added.“I am courting arrest because democracy is being murdered. Are we not even allowed to protest peacefully? We are putting ourselves through hardship to raise our concerns, but instead of listening to us, they have cut off the electricity and water. Even the British never did this. ”The latest protest follows a 15-day agitation in July, led largely by tribal women, after which the administration had assured protesters that eligible and genuinely displaced families would be transparently included in compensation and rehabilitation lists.However, the protesters claimed that they did not get the promised compensation. Also, their houses were now inundated, with two to three feet of water entering homes in several villages which now stand waterlogged including Mandalia, Tapariya and Kuwarpur."The families whose houses have been submerged are so poor that they have been forced to continue living there, or put up one makeshift shelter next to another, and then another. Earlier, the water would rise by half a foot at a time. But this time there was heavy rain on the 26th and 27th of September, followed by a 24-hour red alert, leaving them with no time to move. The villages turned into islands,” said Bhatnagar.The protesters claim that the compensation process remains incomplete, with several families receiving only Rs 5 lakh despite the government announcing a Rs 12.5-lakh package.They are also opposing the compensation conditions, which makes several tribals ineligible for relief.“The cut-off date under Section 11 has been set as 2018, which means people who are now 25-26 years old have received nothing. Those who are older are getting only Rs 5 lakh. What are families with eight or 10 children supposed to do?" asked Bhatnagar, adding that they were not against development projects, but that this development should not come at the cost of the rights of tribals.Bhatnagar pointed to Section 38 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which he said raised concerns about any displacement or submergence taking place before compensation and rehabilitation obligations had been fulfilled.“Villages and homes are now submerged. Houses have started collapsing and water has entered them. Yet, Section 38 of the 2013 law says that compensation for an irrigation project should be paid six months before submergence. If the houses were submerged two months ago, compensation should have been paid eight months earlier,” he said.The authorities, on the other hand, claim that they have been conducting fresh surveys and distributing compensation to affected families. TOI reached out to Chhatarpur district magistrate and is still awaiting a response from the administration.The Majhgawan dam project aims to transfer surplus water from Ken river to Betwa through the Daudhan Dam, a network of tunnels and a 221-km canal. It is supposed to address water shortages in drought-prone Bundelkhand region that spans across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.The project traces back to a plan introduced in 1980 and cleared in 2021 to connect the rivers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid its foundation stone in December 2024.The project is expected to improve agricultural output, curb migration and strengthen groundwater recharge through the revival of traditional Chandela-era ponds.
Article Summary: Tribal families living in the path of the project have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations. The protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.

Article Title: Switch to cleaner fuel: Study calls for tech-neutral stance
Article Text:
Switch to cleaner fuel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi has the strongest CNG infrastructure among the cities assessed in a TERI study and, along with Bengaluru, also has relatively strong EV infrastructure.The study, supported by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), found that effective charging capacity was considerably lower in Lucknow, Guwahati, Dhanbad and Chamba. It said infrastructure readiness was a key determinant of the timing of the transition and that national transition pathways needed regionally differentiated implementation strategies.The “Study on Comparative Assessment of Vehicular Fuels in India’s Energy Transition” examined petrol, diesel, CNG, electricity and LNG across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, private and commercial four-wheelers, light commercial vehicles (LCVs) and heavy-duty vehicles. It covered Delhi, Mumbai, Mumbai Port, Surat, Ahmedabad, Guwahati, Lucknow, Bengaluru, Dhanbad and Chamba.The study found that India should not adopt one fuel or technology as a universal replacement, with different technologies performing different roles across vehicle fleets, applications and stages of the transition.It found that EVs currently provide the lowest ownership costs for two-wheelers and three-wheelers, while CNG offers a relatively balanced and deployment-ready mobility solution across a wide range of personal and commercial applications.The study said CNG has a strong position in passenger cars, taxis, buses and LCVs, while LNG remains particularly relevant for long-haul freight.The study was based partly on a primary survey of 2,315 vehicle owners and drivers across 10 locations, using stratified random sampling. The survey covered vehicle usage, travel distance, mileage, infrastructure access, fuel and maintenance expenditure, technology preferences and willingness to retrofit.Economic considerations emerged as the strongest factor in the assessment, accounting for 31.49% of the overall weighting, followed by environmental considerations at 22.34% and technical factors at 21.25%. The report said the weights reflected the importance of affordability, ownership cost and operating economics in technology selection.The study said CNG-powered vehicles have the lowest overall life-cycle emissions among the fuel options assessed for several passenger and commercial vehicle segments. It also said environmental performance cannot be judged solely through tailpipe emissions, with EV performance influenced by electricity generation, battery manufacturing and material requirements.The findings come amid a continuing debate over the role of vehicles and fuels in Delhi-NCR’s air pollution and the effectiveness of past interventions. Tarun Kapoor, advisor to PM, said better data was needed to guide policy. “Good authentic data is very urgently needed. Whatever interventions we’ve done in the past, it’s been like hitting in the dark and the results have not really been the way it was thought,” he said.The study also said electrification changes rather than eliminates energy-security risks by shifting some dependence from petroleum towards electricity infrastructure, critical minerals, imported automobile components and battery supply chains.“The real policy question is not which fuel should replace all others, but rather which fuel is best suited for which application, under what operating conditions and at what stage of India’s transition journey,” said AK Tiwari, member, PNGRB.The study recommended a technology-neutral framework at the national level, with differentiated approaches based on vehicle segment, region and application. It also called for accelerated CNG infrastructure development, greater use of CBG and differentiated CNG and LNG strategies, with LNG focused on long-haul mobility.
Article Summary: Delhi has the strongest CNG infrastructure among the cities assessed in a TERI study. Bengaluru also has relatively strong EV infrastructure. Study found that effective charging capacity was considerably lower in Lucknow, Guwahati, Dhanbad and Chamba.

Article Title: Ram Temple donation row: SC to hear plea against Champat Rai on Nov 2 over alleged irregularities
Article Text:
The Supreme Court has agreed to hear on November 2 a plea filed by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai

What is the case?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to hear on November 2 plea filed by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai and others over alleged irregularities in donations and land transactions linked to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.According to news agency ANI, the plea alleges that donations collected for the construction of the temple were misappropriated and that land was illegally purchased in areas surrounding the temple.The plea also seeks the dissolution of the existing Trust and its complete reconstitution.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the petition would be taken up along with other pending pleas concerning the same.Earlier, Rai had been given a clean chit by the UP-State SIT, which probed the donation theft. He is listed in the chargesheet as a key prosecution witness. Chargesheet names as accused only eight arrested counting agents and employees for criminal breach of trust and corruption.Rai informed investigators that he first learned of the irregularities via a phone call and video message while travelling. He subsequently reviewed CCTV footage and suggested lodging the formal police complaint.The alleged misappropriation of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya has triggered a political and administrative controversy. The issue came to light on June 7, when former Samajwadi Party MLA Pawan Pandey alleged that around Rs 7-7.5 crore from the daily offerings made by devotees had been siphoned off. He alleged that people associated with the temple’s management were involved in the alleged misappropriation.The allegations soon gained political traction after SP chief Akhilesh Yadav backed the claims and sought accountability. A section of local BJP leaders also called for an investigation, putting the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, which manages the temple, under increased scrutiny.The concerns grew after Nripendra Misra, chairman of the temple construction committee and a trust member, flagged loopholes in the existing system for handling and counting cash donations. He recommended appointing a professional CEO to strengthen oversight and transparency.Trust general secretary Champat Rai initially rejected the allegations. However, amid mounting scrutiny, the trust sought an investigation by the Uttar Pradesh government.The SIT submitted an interim report within a week, flagging procedural weaknesses in the system used to manage temple donations and recommending structural reforms to strengthen monitoring and accountability.The probe subsequently led to arrests in connection with the alleged irregularities.
Article Summary: Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeks legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai. The plea alleges that donations collected for the construction of the temple were misappropriated and that land was illegally purchased in areas surrounding the temple.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total 1 China 132 53 45 230 2 Japan 41 68 63 172 3 South Korea 21 26 43 90 4 Uzbekistan 12 17 13 42 5 Kazakhstan 9 13 23 45 6 Thailand 9 8 13 30 7 Bahrain 9 2 3 14 8 Iran 8 15 9 32 9 North Korea 7 5 5 17 10 Malaysia 6 3 9 18 11 Hong Kong 5 12 17 34 12 INDIA 4 20 21 45

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: LPG price hike: 19-kg commercial cylinder gets Rs 62.50 costlier; new Aadhaar rule kicks in for domestic users
Article Text:
Commercial LPG gets costlier

The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1, taking the price to Rs 2,810. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137 per litre.The changes come as domestic LPG consumers face a new requirement from October 1, 2026. Those seeking to book refills at the regulated Retail Selling Price (RSP) with applicable subsidy will now need to have completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA).The authentication requirement is aimed at ensuring that subsidised LPG reaches genuine and deserving households. Each LPG connection is linked to an Aadhaar-authenticated consumer to prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use, remove duplicate and ineligible connections, and make subsidy delivery more targeted and transparent.Consumers who have already completed BAA will not need to repeat the process and can continue booking refills as before. Those who have not completed it will be able to book a refill at the RSP with subsidy once their authentication is completed.Consumers can complete the authentication process through several channels. During refill delivery, the delivery person can carry out BAA on the spot using the OMC mobile application.The process can also be completed by visiting the LPG distributor's showroom. Consumers can alternatively complete it themselves from home through their OMC's mobile application: IndianOil ONE for Indane customers, HelloBPCL for Bharatgas customers and HP PAY for HP Gas customers.Consumers who are unwilling or unable to complete BAA can still receive LPG. They will have to register their choice through their OMC's digital channels, including the consumer web portal, mobile app, WhatsApp chatbot, IVRS or other available channels.In such cases, LPG will be supplied at the applicable market price without subsidy, in 5-kg or 10-kg cylinders, subject to local availability with the OMC.Consumers who have not yet completed BAA have been urged to do so through any of the available channels, which are accessible in both urban and rural areas.
Article Summary: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137.

Article Title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gautam Gambhir questions Guwahati pitch after India chase 406 with ease
Article Text:
India's coach Gautam Gambhir, left, chats with captain Shubman Gill during a practice session. (AP Photo)

‘It’s not fair for the bowlers’

Gambhir backs exposure for young bowlers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was far less impressed by the conditions that allowed both teams to score more than 400 runs.After West Indies posted 405 for seven, India chased down the target in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets to seal the three-match ODI series 2-0. Shubman Gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 as India completed the highest successful run chase in their ODI history.Yet, for Gambhir, the remarkable numbers also highlighted a concern. He felt the pitch offered too little to the bowlers and called for a greater balance between bat and ball.“Look, if I have to be absolutely honest, I feel I think there has to be a bit of more contest between bat and ball, because I think you talk about cricket - but this is not cricket, this is only batting,” Gambhir told Star Sports after the match.“Because imagine a young bowler bowling on this wicket, and the opposition getting 400 and then we go on to chase 400. Obviously, for the records it's outstanding, for the crowd it's outstanding, for the broadcaster it's outstanding, but if you ask me as a genuine cricket fan and as a coach, because I have to have sympathy for the bowlers as well.”“When you bowl on this kind of a wicket, it's not fair for the bowlers. So we've got to give something to the bowlers so there's at least something which the bowlers can work with,” he added.The Guwahati surface produced a stunning batting display, with West Indies reaching 405 for seven before India responded with 406 for two.John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo struck centuries for West Indies, while Gill and Rohit then led the Indian chase. Gill's unbeaten 223 was the defining innings of the day, while his opening partnership of 255 with Rohit was India's second-highest in men's ODIs. Virat Kohli , who had scored a century in the first ODI, contributed 29 off 19 balls before falling, while Ruturaj Gaikwad made 31 off 37.The match became only the second successful chase of a target of 400 or more in men's ODI history, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in 2006.For Gambhir, however, the scale of the scoring made it important to consider what the conditions meant for the bowlers rather than simply celebrating the batting numbers.“The first thing is that you need some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers,” he said.“Often you can't be hard on bowlers, because sometimes bowling figures are such that they haven't bowled as poorly as their figures suggest. Because the margin is very small.”He also pointed to the restrictions modern-day bowlers face in ODI cricket, including fielding restrictions, two new balls and the increasing power of batters.“Plus, I think you can only bowl in good areas because besides that, with five fielders inside, two new balls, and the kind of power-hitting there is now, bowlers don't really have many options,” Gambhir said.“That is why, as a coach, as a support staff, the first thing you look at is, were they able to execute their bowling or their plans properly? If they were able to do that, then you shouldn't be hard on them.”“If you get too hard just looking at their analysis, then we will never be able to develop bowlers.”India gave Auqib Nabi his ODI debut despite already leading the series 1-0, and Gambhir said putting inexperienced bowlers into difficult situations was an important part of India's preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“Imagine Auqib [Nabi] playing his first game... somewhere you need to give them a bit of support and keep a bit of an extra cushion or extra options for them,” he said. “But unfortunately, today there wasn't much for any bowler.”Gambhir said India could have waited until the third ODI, when the series would already be decided, to give Nabi an opportunity. But he argued that a dead rubber would not recreate the pressure young players could experience at a World Cup.“We could have given Auqib a chance in the next match too when it's a dead rubber, but in a dead rubber, you don't have that pressure which comes with the pressure of winning a series,” he said.“And we all know that the World Cup is all about pressure. Cricket isn't going to change like that, only the pressure will be different because the World Cup comes once in four years, so we want to put bowlers under pressure.”He also cited Gurnoor Brar as an example of a young bowler who could benefit from being exposed to demanding phases of an ODI.“For example, Gurnoor [Brar]. Having Gurnoor bowl in the first 10 overs, bowling at the death, I know people will talk about his analysis, but the more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said.“Because you can have him bowl in the middle overs and get good analysis or good stats for him, make him bowl defensively, but the more we expose them at such times, the better it is for Indian cricket.”
Article Summary: India coach Gautam Gambhir unhappy with conditions in Guwahati. Both West Indies and India scored more than 400 runs in Wednesday's match. India chased down the target in 43.3 overs to win by eight wickets. Shubman Gill hit an unbeaten 223 as India won the match by eight runs.

He said the party's election manifesto would include several measures for farmers.On his recent visit to Raebareli and allegations of police misconduct involving SP MLA Rahul Lodhi, Yadav questioned how police could behave in such a manner with an elected representative.“How can police behave like this with an elected representative?” he asked.He also said, “This time, it will be Lodhi versus (Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister) Yogi (Adityanath).”Yadav further said Uttar Pradesh's proposed target of becoming a USD 1-trillion economy could not be achieved through corruption, saying, “A USD-1-trillion economy will not be built through theft of offerings.”He also said the SP would continue to focus on farmers, recalling former prime minister Chaudhary Charan Singh and farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

Article Title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Text:

What happened inside the cockpit

NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft. He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.Also read: Passengers recall harrowing ordeal on flight that nearly crashed The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.Later, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilots became involved in a physical altercation as the flight approached Israel. “During the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot,” Netanyahu said in a video address.“Apparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.” Netanyahu added “almost all” passengers were Israelis, with some passengers and crew members breaking into the cockpit and subduing the attacker. “I spoke with one of the Israeli passengers. He told me that the plane went into a spin and began to dive. He told me that somehow he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and together they neutralized the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraft’s systems,” Netanyahu said. “Another air crew that was on the plane entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane,” he added. He also praised those who intervened, saying: “I salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.”Also read: Israel security minister on flydubai cockpit incident Flydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely."Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.Read more: Passenger's mother says pilot tried to kill co-pilot on Flydubai flight The airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.The investigation is continuing, with Israeli authorities examining the circumstances of the cockpit confrontation, the alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft and the security clearance given to the crew.
Article Summary: Indian pilot identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai. He intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it. The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.

NEW DELHI: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday praised Indian flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery after he was seriously injured in a cockpit altercation that forced a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Netanyahu met passengers after they returned to Israel and said the actions of Machchhar, passengers and crew had helped avert a major disaster.“My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery. Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster,” Netanyahu said in a post.“He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals. I wish Captain Machchhar a speedy and full recovery. He is a true hero,” he said.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said Machchhar was receiving treatment at a hospital in Tabuk and was in stable condition.“Our Embassy in Riyadh and Consulate in Jeddah have been following the health condition of Mr Smit Machchhar, the brave Indian pilot of Flydubai flight that was diverted to Tabuk today,” it said in a post on X.“A full update on his health is awaited but he is reported to be in stable condition,” the embassy said, adding that it was in contact with his family and Saudi authorities.The embassy said it would continue to follow up on his health and provide all possible assistance for his wellbeing.Netanyahu met passengers after a rescue flight carrying around 180 people, most of them Israelis, landed at Ben Gurion International Airport.Describing the episode as an “extremely serious security incident”, Netanyahu praised the passengers and crew members who intervened during the flight. He said they had shown “exceptional resourcefulness and courage” and “saved many lives” by preventing what he described as a major disaster.Netanyahu also said the pilot accused of attacking the other pilot had been arrested and was being interrogated by Saudi authorities.Israeli passenger Yaniv, who was among those who intervened, later told Netanyahu that he entered the cockpit and found the alleged attacker at the aircraft's controls.“When I went in, I saw the terrorist on the controls, between the two seats. There were no pilots in the seats,” Yaniv said, according to The Times of Israel.He said he pulled the man away from the controls and called on other passengers to restrain him. When he realised the aircraft was tilting sharply, Yaniv said he returned to the cockpit and pulled back on the controls until the aircraft began to level out.He said he knew what to do because “I watch Mayday”, referring to the aviation accident documentary series.“The plane started leveling out a little more, and then the pilot told me he was taking over from there,” he said.Another passenger, Tzika Manes, told Israel's Channel 12 that he and two other Israeli passengers helped subdue the alleged attacker.Manes said his wife had heard screams and sounds of a struggle near the cockpit and alerted a flight attendant. He said passengers were thrown around the cabin as the aircraft lost altitude.The three passengers eventually restrained the alleged attacker using corded headphones, with the effort taking around 20 to 25 minutes, according to Manes.A doctor travelling on the flight also helped treat the injured pilot, he said.The flydubai flight was diverted to Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia and made an emergency landing there.The passengers were subsequently flown back to Israel on a rescue flight. The Israel Airports Authority had earlier set up a dedicated waiting and information area at Ben Gurion Airport for relatives of those on board.Netanyahu's office said the situation had been brought under control and that Israeli authorities were working to ensure the passengers' safe return.Israel scrambled fighter jets after concerns that the aircraft could have been hijacked, according to reports citing Israeli officials.The incident prompted security consultations in Israel, while authorities maintained contact with Saudi officials over the passengers and the investigation.An Israeli official described the episode as a “severe disaster” that had been averted.Flydubai confirmed that flight FZ1073, travelling from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion Airport, had experienced an incident and landed safely in Tabuk.“Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities,” the airline said.The airline did not provide details of the cockpit altercation.The incident involved an altercation between the pilots while the aircraft was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.An Israeli official told AP that one of the pilots was armed with a knife. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit.The captain and first officer were injured and taken to hospital, according to Tabuk airport authorities cited by Saudi state television.Netanyahu said the evidence indicated that one pilot had stabbed the other and apparently attempted to crash the aircraft.Publicly available flight-tracking data showed that the aircraft transmitted an emergency alert around two-and-a-half hours after departing Dubai and subsequently dropped sharply from about 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet within roughly a minute before making an erratic turn near the Jordanian border.The circumstances of the cockpit altercation remain under investigation.Saudi authorities are questioning the alleged attacker, while Israeli authorities are examining the security implications of the incident and are expected to question passengers after their return.Transport minister Miri Regev asked Israel's Civil Aviation Authority to investigate what she described as an alleged violation of the aviation agreement between Israel and the UAE. She also called for flydubai flights to Israel to be suspended.Israeli media reported that Machchhar was of Indian origin and that the other pilot was reportedly Omani. Those nationality details had not been independently confirmed by flydubai.Reports also said a second team of pilots in civilian clothes was aboard the aircraft and helped prevent one of the pilots from taking control, though that detail had not been independently confirmed.The investigation remains underway, with flydubai saying it is working with the relevant authorities.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national based in Dubai, was reportedly stabbed and severely wounded during the incident. According to Israeli reports, he intervened after an alleged attempt to crash the aircraft. Israel scrambled fighter jets after concerns that the aircraft could have been hijacked, according to reports.

Article Title: What makes a rape case 'rarest of rare'? How courts decide on the death penalty
Article Text:
Should death penalty remain exception in rape cases, not the rule?

And should death remain an exception rather than the rule?

Why women's safety is back at the centre of debate

2026 witness​es shocking incidents of sexual assault

When does rape become 'rarest of rare'?

Activist Yogita Bhayana in conversation with TOI

What changes when the accused is a minor?

Minor victims in rape cases in India: NCRB data

Does a harsher sentence always mean justice?

Two cases with different court sentences

Why tougher laws alone may not be enough

Delhi University students take out protest march amid rains to Miranda House college in north campus over women safety after Kalkaji gang rape.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every time a brutal rape case shocks the country, the demand returns almost immediately: give the harshest possible punishment.The anger is understandable. But the law applies a much narrower test. Not every rape case, however grave, crosses the threshold for the death penalty.India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025.The figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country bringing questions of punishment, deterrence and justice back into focus.While Indian law provides for stringent punishment, including the death penalty in certain rape cases, capital punishment remains restricted to specific circumstances.So when does a rape case cross the legal threshold for the ultimate punishment? What makes one case “rarest of rare”, while another results in life imprisonment?A series of recent cases has once again put women’s safety under scrutiny.In September, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by three men posing as police personnel at Astha Kunj Park near Kalkaji Mandir in Delhi. The case triggered student protests demanding stronger measures for women’s safety, and police arrested the accused.In August, another 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped by a bus driver and conductor after boarding a bus from Greater Noida. She was later dropped near Kashmere Gate. The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of the case and sought reports from authorities.Against this backdrop, the Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of recent rape incidents in Delhi-NCR, flagging what it described as a "systematic failure" to ensure basic public safety.Concerns have extended beyond Delhi.In Bihar, three incidents involving alleged sexual harassment and assault were reported within days. In Jamui, a teenage boy and girl were allegedly stopped and assaulted by a group of men on September 19, with three accused arrested after a video surfaced online. In Samastipur, a minor girl was allegedly assaulted and molested, while another case in Banka’s Mandar Hill area involved allegations of a woman being harassed and her male friend assaulted.The cases have also spilled onto the streets. Students and young people in the national capital are holding protests demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability.Indian law permits the death penalty in certain aggravated rape cases, including those involving minors and cases where the victim dies or is left in a persistent vegetative state, under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act.But the existence of the death penalty does not mean it follows automatically in the most brutal cases.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said courts consider factors including the brutality of the offence, injuries caused, the vulnerability of the survivor and the long-term consequences while determining punishment.Rupali Jain, who practises in the high court and Supreme Court, said the harm caused by rape, while grave, cannot by itself justify capital punishment."As harm is inherent in every rape, it cannot alone justify death. The court must also apply the 'criminal test', the offender’s age, antecedents, background, custodial conduct and prospects of reform, as reiterated in Manoj v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2022)," she said.The "rarest of rare" doctrine gained renewed attention following the 2012 Nirbhaya case . On December 16, 2012, a 23-year-old woman was gang-raped and brutally assaulted inside a moving bus in Delhi. She died from her injuries days later.Four adult accused were sentenced to death by the trial court in 2013. The Delhi high court upheld the punishment in 2014, and the Supreme Court confirmed the death sentences in 2017, holding that the case fell within the “rarest of rare” category.However, the Supreme Court has also held that the brutality or heinousness of an offence alone does not automatically make it a "rarest of rare" case. Courts must weigh aggravating circumstances against mitigating factors, including the possibility of reform and rehabilitation.But the death penalty is not automatic, even in cases involving extreme violence.The Bilkis Bano case offers another example of how courts apply the 'rarest of rare' test differently.In the Bilkis Bano case, 11 men were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment for gang rape, murder and other offences linked to the 2002 Gujarat riots. Bilkis was 21 and five months pregnant when she was raped, and several members of her family were killed.The case shows why the "rarest of rare" test is not based only on how brutal or shocking a crime appears. Courts must also consider other factors, including the background of the accused and whether there is any possibility of reform.Activist Yogita Bhayana, however, argues that the impact of rape on the survivor should receive greater weight when courts consider the threshold."Every rape case is rarest of the rare in terms of the victim," she said, arguing that the legal system can focus heavily on physical brutality while overlooking the lasting impact on survivors.Bhayana said she believes the death penalty should remain available in rape cases and argued for greater weight to be given to the consequences of the crime for survivors while deciding punishment.Jain, too, stressed the need for severe punishment, while emphasising that its deterrent effect depends on certainty and speed of enforcement."In my opinion, the most effective way to deter sexual violence is stern punishment, imposed swiftly and with certainty. The offender must know that the consequence is severe and unavoidable: imprisonment for the remainder of natural life and, in the rarest of cases, death. The statute already provides for this, as Sections 65, 66, 70 and 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 prescribe natural-life imprisonment or death for the gravest forms. The deficit lies in enforcement."The legal process changes significantly when the accused is under 18.Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a child aged between 16 and 18 who is accused of a “heinous offence”, including rape, can undergo a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board.The Board looks at the child’s mental and physical capacity to commit the offence, whether they understood its consequences and the circumstances in which the alleged offence took place.Depending on that assessment, the case can be transferred to the Children’s Court, which then decides whether the child should be tried as an adult.Rupali Jain said the existing law already provides a framework for dealing with serious offences committed by juveniles, and the focus should remain on how it is implemented rather than simply lowering the age threshold.She also pointed out that the Juvenile Justice Act bars the death penalty and life imprisonment without the possibility of release for a child in conflict with law.However, activist Yogita Bhayana argues that the distinction between different degrees of brutality can be deeply troubling for survivors.“The miner will be treated as miner unless he brutally kills her, rape her in a very gruesome manner. Then otherwise, it will not be in the rarest of the rare category. So we need to change the whole thing,” she said, arguing that the system should focus more closely on the impact of the crime on the survivor and called for greater awareness and stronger mechanisms to deal with sexual offences.For survivors, justice does not necessarily end with an arrest, conviction or sentence.Activist Yogita Bhayana said the distinction between "high-profile" and ordinary rape cases often comes from media attention rather than the nature of the crime or the survivor’s experience."There is no case which is high profile. What becomes media-highlighted becomes high profile," she said, pointing out that even Nirbhaya came from a humble, lower-middle-class family.She said survivors often continue to deal with trauma, repeated questioning and the pressures of the legal process long after public attention has moved on."Attention doesn’t mean justice," Bhayana said.Dr Vinodh Sreeram, senior psychiatrist & addiction specialist at Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru, said rape can deeply alter a survivor’s sense of safety, relationships and ability to return to everyday life.He cautioned against judging trauma only by visible injuries or by how brutal an assault appears. Two survivors of similar incidents can experience very different psychological effects depending on factors such as age, past experiences, their relationship with the accused and the support available to them."The absence of visible injury should never be mistaken for the absence of psychological trauma," he said.On whether the death penalty can provide psychological closure, Sreeram said there is no single answer. Some survivors or families may see a severe sentence as justice, but "closure rarely comes from the sentence alone".Being believed, treated with dignity, protected from further harm and supported through recovery can be just as important, he said. Repeated questioning, cross-examination, delays and prolonged appeals can themselves become additional sources of distress.Recent protests in Delhi have again brought demands for safer public spaces, stronger policing, better surveillance and greater accountability to the forefront.Advocate Sumit Nagpal said the biggest challenge is not necessarily the absence of laws, but the capacity to enforce them."The bottleneck is capacity, not the statute. India has roughly twenty judges per million people against a recommended fifty, and police strength sits well below sanctioned levels in most states. Until that gap closes, every reform stays on paper," he said."So the real agenda is unglamorous: more investigators, more courts, more forensic capacity, fewer vacancies. No amendment will substitute for that."Activist Yogita Bhayana said the biggest gap remains implementation. While reforms, awareness and gender-sensitisation efforts have increased, she said survivors continue to face inadequate support, delays in fast-track courts and a lack of sensitivity within the system.She also warned that repeated exposure to sexual-violence cases can make institutions become "immune" to such crimes."For them, they see it like an everyday thing," she said, arguing that continued training and sensitisation are needed to ensure sexual violence is not treated as routine.Dr Vinodh Sreeram said debates around harsher punishment must also account for the realities of reporting, particularly because many survivors know the accused and may face fear, stigma and family pressure.A trauma-informed justice system, he said, should focus on sensitive questioning, privacy, timely trials and access to psychological support.“Justice is not only about the severity of punishment. It is also about ensuring that survivors are heard, protected, treated with dignity and given the opportunity to rebuild their lives,” Sreeram said.The death penalty is only one part of the debate. The larger challenge is to prevent such crimes, ensure quicker justice and make sure survivors get the support they need.
Article Summary: India recorded 29,536 rape cases in 2024, according to the latest National Crime Records Bureau data. In Delhi, 1,058 rape cases were registered that year, while Delhi Police reported 1,901 cases in 2025. Figures come amid renewed attention on sexual violence, with a series of recent cases in Delhi and across the country.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The rainy season in India technically ended on Wednesday, with the summer (southwest) monsoon rainfall during June-Sept period recording a deficit of nearly 13% - a level of shortfall which is considered a drought. Significantly, this is the fourth lowest seasonal rainfall since 2001 and the 13th lowest since 1901.The situation is likely to be better during winter when northeast monsoon hits south Peninsular India between Oct 15 and Oct 21, with the IMD predicting 'normal' rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region, Kerala and south interior Karnataka during Oct-Dec period. However, the winter monsoon will bring cheer to limited regions.Though most other parts of India are expected to receive 'below-normal' rainfall during the Oct-Dec period, some areas of northwest India (Punjab, parts of Haryana, Uttarakhand, Himachal and J&K) and southern parts of peninsular India are likely to get "normal to above-normal" rainfall. Incidentally, Punjab and peninsular India had to face huge rainfall deficit during the summer monsoon season, which led to drought in many districts.Overall, south Peninsular India receives 30% of its annual rainfall during northeast (winter) monsoon season. TN, Puducherry and Karaikal receive 48% of their annual rainfall during northeast monsoon season. So, normal winter monsoon this year may bring relief to the region, which received the fourth lowest summer monsoon rainfall since 1901.“We cannot forecast exact date of arrival of winter monsoon in south Peninsula at this stage. It generally coincides with final withdrawal of summer monsoon and may hit the region any day during Oct 15-21,” said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra. Though India as a whole received nearly 13% less than normal rainfall, east and northeast India faced the highest deficit of 25%, followed by south Peninsula (24%), northwest India (6%) and central India (3%). Mohapatra said there has been a recent trend of east & northeast India consistently reporting decrease in rainfall.
Article Summary: Winter rain may bring relief to southern India. IMD predicts 'normal' rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema region. Punjab and peninsular India had to face huge rainfall deficit during the summer monsoon season, which led to drought.

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc, led by the Congress, has announced a mega action plan to take forward its campaign against “vote chori” and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The key stakeholders of the INDIA bloc met today in the national capital to chalk out a roadmap for nationwide protests against the Election Commission’s “flawed and partisan” approach.The INDIA bloc's renewed offensive comes days after an Indian Express report citing internal differences within the Election Commission of India (ECI) regarding the implementation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and modifications to voter registration processes. The opposition parties' meeting also comes in the backdrop of successful mobilisation programmed led by the Cockroach Janata Party against NEET paper leak, which brought the GenZ to the streets and forced the government to accept their demands.After hours long deliberations, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge unveiled the opposition’s blueprint for intensified demonstrations against EC’s ‘malpractices’ and shared details of how the INDIA bloc will stand up against electoral irregularities.Here is what the INDIA bloc allies decided on their action plan against EC’s ‘partisan approach and malpractices’Then there was also a list of 6 demands which the opposition parties announced. It includedSo far, so good. But the problem is that all these demands have already been raised by various opposition parties from time to time without any success.We have heard several leaders in the past demanding a return to ballot paper. This has not happened and is unlikely to happen.The fight over alleged discrepancies in the SIR process has been an ongoing one. We have seen Rahul Gandhi and other regional leaders raise the issue. But none of them have managed to sustain the momentum or stop the process. Even the courts have refused to back their allegations and have not stopped the SIR process.Now, let’s focus on the action plan.Protests at district level, march to Election Commission’s office, rallies, appeal in Supreme Court - all make for good optics, but can they bring about enough pressure?The Congress, which is leading the opposition block, has been consistent in raising these issues, but has failed to keep the momentum going. Rahul Gandhi has addressed several press conferences in the last two years leading the charge against the Election Commission and Gyanesh Kumar. His yatra in Bihar ahead of assembly elections last year brought the issue to centre stage but once again the momentum did not sustain.Clearly, the Congress and the other opposition parties need to think how to run a sustained campaign for mobilisation.At the CWC meeting held on Tuesday, ahead of today’s INDIA bloc meeting, Rahul Gandhi had claimed that revelations about the Election Commission were now coming out in the open because of the Congress. During the two-and-a-half hour CWC meeting, Rahul pointed out that the Congress had been raising the "vote chori" issue strongly with facts and talked about irregularities in polls in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra but many were sceptical of it.Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha claimed that EVM and voters' list "match-fixing" of polls was underway in the country and asserted that his party should not budge from the path of "virodh" (opposing) as well as "pratirodh" (resistance) against it from streets to Parliament.Rahul Verma, political scientist and a Fellow at New Delhi-based think tank Centre for Policy Research, feels that the Congress needs to be persistent and have patience.“One of the reasons why the congress fails to do mobilization is that they raise important issues but are not persistent. They need to have patience. Congress has been talking about all the important issues but did not sit on a protest like the CJP,” Rahul Verma says.“Even the CJP would not have thought of the success they eventually got. They continued sitting on protest even when there was little traction in their favour. Eventually, they managed to mobilise a lot of support and forced the government to concede to their demands,” Rahul Verma adds.If the INDIA bloc meeting was about showcasing opposition unity, well the purpose was at best half achieved. There were more questions on INDIA bloc’s united presence than answers. The BJP has aggressively highlighted the division within the opposition ranks. With several regional parties openly against the Congress, the BJP leaders have been quick to question Rahul Gandhi’s acceptance as the leader of the opposition block.BJP national media incharge Ashish Usha Agarwal questioned Rahul Gandhi’s leadership of the INDIA bloc and said the outcomes of the INDIA bloc meeting on Wednesday were "zero vision, 100 per cent frustration.The BJP claimed that the meeting was an advance excuse for poll defeats, with the leaders of the opposition grouping rejecting Rahul Gandhi's leadership."The INDI Alliance fell apart even before the meeting took place. The DMK did not attend the meeting. Akhilesh was busy elsewhere. The AAP had already declined," Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said at a press conference at the BJP headquarters.“Why is this happening? It is because the INDI Alliance is simply not willing to accept Rahul Gandhi as its leader. When Mamata Banerjee said the opposition had taken these matters to the Election Commission and the Supreme Court and "knocked on every possible door," it was an admission of the fact that the old ways had failed. The meeting today discussed the need for mobilisation on the ground by involving the civil society along with the political fight.The Congress has kept an arm’s distance from the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP). SRINAGAR/ NEW DELHI: In a joint operation by Army, police and security forces, a top Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif, alias Hashim Musa, was killed in an overnight encounter in the upper reaches of Yousmarg, around 60km from Srinagar.With his elimination, the entire group of four LeT commanders who had been operating in J&K since 2022 and were also behind the Pahalgam massacre has been wiped out. Home ministry called it a massive victory. Intelligence agencies had been tracking for two years the whereabouts of this former Pak Special Service Group (SSG) commando who had infiltrated into the Valley.Neutralisation of Musa is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in J&K,” the ministry said in a statement. This group was responsible for a string of sensational and deadly attacks across the region. The Musa-led squad’s terror trail included the Kandi attack in Rajouri (May 2023) where five Army personnel were killed, the Halan attack (Aug 2023), and the Dera Ki Gali ambush (Dec 2023) where terrorists targeted two Army vehicles, killing several soldiers.The group also orchestrated the June 9, 2024 attack on a bus carrying Hindu pilgrims in Reasi, killing nine and wounding 40. They were linked to the Oct 2024 Gagangir attack in Ganderbal, which claimed the lives of seven, and the Bootapathri attack near Gulmarg that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The violent spree culminated in the devastating April 2025 Baisaran Valley attack in Pahalgam, where the terrorists massacred 26 tourists and a local horseman.

Article Title: Supreme Court allows sale, manufacture of next-generation green firecrackers
Article Text:
Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Supreme Court on Wednesday paved the way for the manufacture and sale of next-generation joined green firecrackers after Centre's recommendation. Commonly known as 'ladi', these were earlier banned by the court.SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that while the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned, the activity would not be allowed at all hours.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale that government had recommended that joined firecrackers, which complied with norms fixed by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI), be allowed. The issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15.Submitting the findings of CSIR-NEERI, Bhati said the report said 25 braids were burst in one second in conventional joined firecrackers whereas in next-generation joined firecrackers, only five braids were burst in a second.Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.Advocate Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for some manufacturers, assured the bench they would do so.As the pollution crisis in winter has become an annual affair in Delhi, the bench said it would pass a separate order for the national capital. "We're making this very clear. Neither are we going to agree with you for a total ban nor are we going to allow it 24 hours," the court said.A total ban would have a "sentimental effect", SC said, but allowing bursting of crackers throughout the day would have a "huge impact on every other living being, including old people, sick people and children"."We need to find a solution whereby we can give specified time and we can specify what crackers are to be used," the bench told the petitioner seeking curbs on the sale of firecrackers in NCR.Earlier, two government organisations had taken contradictory stands in SC on allowing next-generation green firecrackers. While CSIR-NEERI approved them saying their pollution levels had decreased by 40-60% and recommended commercial production of flowerpots, sparklers, 'chakkars', pencils, 'ladis' and twinkling stars, Central Pollution Control Board said they contained barium nitrate, which was banned by SC.
Article Summary: Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority. Issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15. SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned at all hours.

NEW DELHI: The full Election Commission - comprising CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - met Wednesday, a second time in five days, and decided to extend the deadlines for the ongoing SIR exercise in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya, reports Bharti Jain.The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in Andhra will now run from July 31 to Oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to Oct 16. For Meghalaya, the date for publication of the final poll roll has been revised to Oct 26.The second full meeting of the commission since an Indian Express report alleged that ECs Sandhu and Joshi had objected to steps taken by EC on 14 occasions over 10 months reaffirms that the CEC and the two ECs have agreed to sit together and transact normal business of the commission through regular meetings.The draft roll of Meghalaya published on Aug 5 listed 21.7 lakh electors, with around 7.7% absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors deleted. In Andhra, the draft roll listed 3.7 crore electors after deleting 10.8% of its electorate.
